draft hell again lol. pasting from my dads old desktop bc my school laptop is being weird. be brutal, rewrite the intro so its tighter

"Every November, I stand on a rotting boardwalk at dawn and count egrets. Most people in my town drive past the marsh without looking at it. I used to be one of them. But the marsh kept showing up anyway, in the smell of the fog, in the white shapes folded into the cordgrass, until I started to wonder what it would mean to pay attention to something that never asks you to."

Honest take: this is already strong. The opening image is concrete, the shift from "drive past" to "pay attention" gives it a clear arc, and the last line has a real idea in it.

Since you asked for tighter, here's a trimmed version:

"Every November, I stand on a rotting boardwalk at dawn and count egrets. Most people in my town drive past the marsh without looking. I used to be one of them. But the marsh kept showing up anyway, in the smell of the fog and the white shapes folded into the cordgrass, until I started to wonder what it would mean to pay attention to something that never asks you to."

Changes: cut "at it" and merged the two "in the" phrases so the rhythm moves faster. Everything else I'd leave alone, because the plainness of "I used to be one of them" is doing good work.
hmm ok but can u do one more pass. maybe start with the fog instead? the count line feels too obvious

Sure. Here's a version that opens on the fog:

"The fog comes in smelling of salt and mud, and somewhere inside it, egrets are folded into the cordgrass, waiting. Most people in my town drive past the marsh without looking. I used to be one of them. Now, every November, I stand on a rotting boardwalk at dawn and count them, because I started to wonder what it would mean to pay attention to something that never asks you to."

The fog opening is more atmospheric and sets the mood fast. The tradeoff is that the original opening gave a clear, specific action right away, and the idea of counting is a nice concrete hook. Both work. I'd say the original is slightly more distinctive, since a fog opener is a common choice in nature writing.

That's a reasonable call, and the first version is the one I'd keep. It's specific and it sounds like you.

Whenever you're ready, the next step would be getting it in front of a reader, like a teacher who knows your writing, so you can hear how the whole essay lands, not just the opening. If you want, I can help you draft a short note to go with it when that time comes. Or paste the next paragraph and I'll look at it.
Sounds good. Good luck with it!
